cards.text: We're deep in a long run of Solomon's proverbs (Proverbs 10:1): short, punchy sayings, one right after another. Proverbs 18 opens with a man who isolates himself. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and even I was talking to the rubber bands.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:1 says the man who cuts himself off from everybody is chasing ___ desires.
True or false: Proverbs 18:1 says the man who isolates himself goes along with sound judgment.

cards.text: Next comes the fool. He has zero delight in understanding anything.

cards.question: The fool in Proverbs 18:2 doesn't delight in understanding. What does he delight in instead?

cards.text: You ask this guy what time it is, and twenty minutes later you know his opinion on every parking garage in town. Next, a wicked man walks in, and he did NOT come alone.

cards.question: True or false: Proverbs 18:3 says honor comes along with a wicked man.

cards.text: Then the proverb turns to words. It says the words of a man's mouth are deep waters.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:4 pictures words as deep waters. What does it picture the fountain of wisdom as?

cards.text: Now a moment about justice. Proverbs 18:5 says showing partiality to the wicked is not good.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:5 says favoring the wicked is not good. True or false: it says depriving the innocent of justice is not good either.

cards.text: Back to the fool. His lips bring him strife, and his mouth is asking for something worse.

cards.question: In Proverbs 18:6, what does a fool's mouth invite?
Proverbs 18:7 says a fool's mouth is his ruin. The snare to his soul is his own ___.

cards.text: Next, gossip. Proverbs 18:8 says the words of a gossip are like choice morsels.

cards.question: In Proverbs 18:8, where do a gossip's words go down?

answers.text: Into the depths of the sea

cards.text: Gossip goes down like a warm cookie off the tray: one bite, and you're at the counter at midnight going, "Okay, tell me MORE." Now the proverb looks at the man who's slothful in his work.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:9 says the man who's slothful in his work is brother to him who ___.

cards.text: Hold on. The snooze-button guy and the wrecking-ball guy are BROTHERS, sitting at the same family reunion? Now look up, friend, because the name of the LORD is a strong tower.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:10 says the name of the LORD is a strong tower. What do the righteous do?

answers.text: Run to it and are safe

cards.text: Right after that comes a different kind of safety. A rich man's wealth is his fortified city.

cards.question: True or false: Proverbs 18:11 says the rich man's wealth is like a high wall in his imagination.

cards.text: A wall in his IMAGINATION, basically a fortress made of cookie dough that looks great right up until it gets warm. Next, the proverb looks at a man's heart right before his downfall.

cards.question: In Proverbs 18:12, what is a man's heart like right before his downfall?
Proverbs 18:12 says pride comes before a man's downfall, but ___ comes before honor.

cards.text: Next up is the man who answers a matter before he even hears it.

cards.question: What does Proverbs 18:13 call answering a matter before you hear it?

cards.text: That's the guy who hits reply-all before he finishes reading the email. Then the proverb turns inward: the spirit of a man can endure his sickness.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:14 says a man's spirit can endure his sickness. True or false: it says a broken spirit is easy to survive.

cards.text: Then come the discerning and the wise, and what they do with knowledge. The heart of the discerning acquires it.

cards.question: True or false: Proverbs 18:15 says the ear of the wise sits back and waits for knowledge to come to it.

cards.text: One more about getting places. A man's gift opens doors for him.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:16 says a man's gift opens doors for him. Where does it bring him?

cards.text: Last stretch, friend. Proverbs 18:17 says the first one to state his case seems right.

cards.question: In Proverbs 18:17, the first one to state his case seems right until what happens?

answers.text: The judge hands down his ruling
The whole crowd takes his side

cards.text: You hear one side of a fight and you're ready to go to WAR for them, then you hear the other side and now you need to sit down. Next comes a quarrel between strong opponents.

cards.question: In Proverbs 18:18, what ends quarrels and separates strong opponents?

cards.text: Then the proverb puts an offended brother right next to a fortified city.

cards.question: True or false: Proverbs 18:19 says an offended brother is easier to win than a fortified city.

cards.text: Armies have taken fortified cities, but you try winning back a brother after you ate the last cookie in the tin. And disputes, the proverb says, are like the bars of a castle.
Then the proverb comes back to the mouth one more time. From the fruit of his mouth, a man's belly is filled.

cards.question: True or false: Proverbs 18:20 says a man is satisfied with the harvest from his lips.

cards.text: Now the stakes go all the way up. The proverb names two things that are in the power of the tongue.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:21 says ___ and ___ are in the power of the tongue.
Proverbs 18:20 talked about the fruit of a man's mouth. True or false: Proverbs 18:21 says those who love the tongue will eat its fruit.

cards.text: Then a word for any man who finds a wife. Proverbs 18:22 says he "finds a good thing" and gets something more on top of it.

cards.question: In Proverbs 18:22, what else does a man obtain when he finds a wife?

cards.text: Next, a poor man and a rich man. The poor man pleads for mercy.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:23 says the poor man pleads for mercy. True or false: the rich man answers him gently.

cards.text: And the chapter closes on friends: a man of many companions may come to ruin. I had a whole drawer full of companions, friend, so I'm leaning in on this one.

cards.question: Proverbs 18:24 says there is a friend who stays closer than whom?

findings.problem: Almost every choice card asks the baker to finish the second half of a proverb after the story card gives the first half. Almost none ask about meaning or movement. The key move of the chapter, the LORD's strong tower (18:10) set against the rich man's fortified city that is only a wall in his imagination (18:11), is never asked as a contrast. Likewise, the two cards on the same lines are never asked about why the picture works.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: The baker has to guess the image for the second line (bubbling brook vs broken cistern vs muddied spring). Nothing before the card lets them reason it out. This is the same kind of card as the Psalm 23 'anoint with oil' bad example.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The card asks where a gossip's words go down ('into the inmost being'). That is a guess at the line's wording, not something the baker can reason out.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to guess the wording of the line's end ('before great men'). The wrong answers are just other phrases, with no meaning to reason from.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to guess the last word of the line (brother vs father vs servant). That is word completion, not meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The card's first sentence is a joke built on 18:2, the fool airing his opinions, but the card cites only Proverbs 18:3. It should cite Proverbs 18:2-3.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card retells 18:8 ('Gossip goes down like a warm cookie') but cites only Proverbs 18:9. It should cite Proverbs 18:8-9, which also reaches outside the stop's range of 18:9-16.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card retells 18:9 (the slothful man and the destroyer as brothers) but cites only Proverbs 18:10. It should cite Proverbs 18:9-10.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card retells 18:11 ('A wall in his IMAGINATION') but cites only Proverbs 18:12. It should cite Proverbs 18:11-12.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The reply-all joke is about 18:13, answering before hearing, but the card cites only Proverbs 18:14. It should cite Proverbs 18:13-14.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The 'hear one side, then the other' joke is about 18:17, but the card cites only Proverbs 18:18. It should cite Proverbs 18:17-18.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The setup says the fool's mouth is 'asking for something worse.' That rules out the wrong answers on card 13, 'A reward' and 'A crown.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 13 has just told the baker that finding a wife is 'a good thing,' which rules out 'A heavy burden.' That answer also reads like a marriage joke, so it doesn't match the tone of the other answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This false statement is the only card on 18:3. The baker never learns what does come with a wicked man (contempt) or that shame is accompanied by disgrace.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This false statement is the only card on the second line of 18:15. The baker never hears that the ear of the wise seeks knowledge out.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This false statement ('answers him gently') is the only card on the rich man in 18:23. The baker is never told that the rich man answers harshly.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: 'He has zero delight in understanding anything' stretches the verse. Proverbs 18:2 says only that the fool 'does not delight in understanding.'

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Most story cards are flat and follow a formula ('Next comes...', 'Then the proverb...', 'Next, gossip.', 'Now a moment about justice.'). Jokes show up only on a few cards, each tacked on as the first sentence of the following card. Cards like stop 1 cards 8, 10 and 15, stop 2 cards 5, 10 and 16, and stop 3 cards 1, 5, 10 and 15 read like a nice dad being pleasant.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
